items.text: Capital Connections · The five questions
What a financing provider asks first, and what a good answer looks like.
The form on this page asks the same five questions, so the introduction arrives with the answers already in hand.
What is the capital for?
What cash flow supports repayment?
What existing debt, receivables or assets affect the need?
What financial information needs preparation?
Where is the business in the process?
What is the capital for?
An acquisition, an ownership transition, growth and working capital, or receivables and assets. The purpose decides the provider, the structure and the paperwork, before any amount does.
What cash flow supports repayment?

Historical adjusted earnings over the debt service after the transaction. A provider underwrites the last fiscal year or the average of the last two, and may not use projections to meet the coverage it requires.
What existing debt, receivables or assets affect the need?
A bank line, an SBA loan, large receivables, equipment. Each one is either collateral or a prior claim, and the provider wants to know which before the first conversation.
What financial information needs preparation?
Statements that are current, statements that need clean-up, or statements that are behind. The answer sets the timeline: a provider cannot underwrite what is not reconciled.
Where is the business in the process?
A signed letter, a target in view, a plan for next year. The stage decides whether the introduction is now or after the preparation work.

items.text: Capital Connections · The rules behind an SBA acquisition loan
What an SBA 7(a) acquisition loan requires, as of October 1, 2026.

The Small Business Administration rewrote its procedure for business acquisitions this year. These are the rules a buyer and a seller meet on a 7(a) acquisition loan, taken from the procedure itself. Capital Row is not a lender and does not package or broker loans.
Maximum 7(a) loan
SBA guarantees 75 percent above $150,000, and 85 percent at or below it.
Equity injection
Of total project cost on an initial acquisition, and it cannot be reduced. A seller note counts toward it only on full standby for the term of the loan, and only up to half.
Independent valuation above
An accredited, independent valuator, engaged by the lender. A valuation prepared for the buyer or the seller may not be used.
Quality of earnings at or above
A report with a cash proof, from an independent financial professional, for the lender, on an initial acquisition or business expansion.
Debt service coverage
Historical earnings over all debt service after the transaction, from the last year or the average of the last two. Projections may not be used.
24 months
The seller may stay, as a consultant
Not as an owner, officer, director or employee. Seller earnouts are prohibited; working capital true-ups are allowed.

SBA, SOP 50 10 8.1, Lender and Development Company Loan Programs, with Technical Policy Updates, effective October 1, 2026, Appendix 15 and Appendix 16. This is information, not advice; the procedure governs, and a lender, an attorney and a CPA should confirm each item before it is relied on.

items.text: Capital Connections · Questions
Plain answers, then a conversation if you want one.
Is Capital Row a lender or a loan broker?
Neither. Capital Row introduces a financing need it has already read to a financing provider, with your permission. The provider handles its application, underwriting and credit decision.
Will you send my financial information to a lender?
Not through this website, and not without your permission. Sensitive information moves through a controlled workspace under a signed engagement.
Does an SBA loan apply to my deal?

The rules are on this page and in full on the Insights note: the loan limit, the equity injection, the seller note, the valuation, the quality of earnings at $3 million. A lender, an attorney and a CPA confirm each item for your deal.
What if the statements are behind?
Then the preparation comes first. A provider cannot underwrite what is not reconciled, and the introduction waits until the story holds.
